problems.title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.notes: BFS beats DFS here — the first leaf you find IS the answer, no need to explore the whole tree

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.notes: canonical BFS; queue + snapshot the queue size at the top of each loop to know where one level ends

problems.title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
problems.notes: same level-order skeleton as 102, aggregate per level instead of collecting — good speed-round warm-up

problems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problems.notes: BFS: take the last node visited per level; or DFS right-first and record the first node seen at each depth

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.notes: multi-source BFS — every rotten orange starts in the queue at level 0, not just a single source

problems.title: 01 Matrix
problems.notes: multi-source BFS from every zero cell simultaneously — much faster than BFS-per-cell from each 1

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.notes: BFS or DFS flood fill both work; interviewer usually wants you to name both and justify which you pick

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.notes: BFS/DFS + a hash map from old node to new node preserves graph structure, including cycles, while cloning

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.notes: BFS over an implicit graph (edges = 1-letter edits); precompute wildcard buckets so you don't rebuild edges at O(n^2*L)
